title: Find Beautiful Indices in the Given Array II
summary: Given a string s and strings a, b, and an integer k, find indices i where s[i:i+len(a)] equals a, s[j:j+len(b)] equals b, and |j - i| is at most k.
statement: Given a string s and strings a, b, and an integer k, find indices i where s[i:i+len(a)] equals a, s[j:j+len(b)] equals b, and |j - i| is at most k. Return these indices in ascending order.
constraints: s, a, and b are lowercase strings and may each contain up to 500,000 characters; k is nonnegative.
Index i must start an occurrence of a and lie within k positions of some start of b.
Return all qualifying a-start indices in ascending order using near-linear matching.
hints: KMP finds overlapping occurrences in linear time, and sorted occurrence starts admit a one-way proximity pointer.
Build prefix arrays for pattern#text for both patterns; scan b starts forward as a starts increase.
For each a start, discard b starts below i-k and accept when the next is at most i+k.
KMP reports every occurrence once; after discarding too-small witnesses none can help a later index, proving the pointer scan complete and linear.
editorial: KMP reports every occurrence once; after discarding too-small witnesses none can help a later index, proving the pointer scan complete and linear.

tests.explanation: KMP finds my at sixteen and thirty-three and squirrel at four and eighteen; both my starts have a nearby witness.
The occurrence at zero matches both patterns and qualifies at distance zero.
